Rules & Origins

About Online Hex Board Game (Hexxagon)

Hexxagon is an iconic strategy board game invented in 1993 by Software Creations. Played on a tessellated hexagonal grid, it challenges players to clone, leap, and infect adjacent opposing tokens.

01

Cell Duplication

Moving 1 distance to an adjacent hex clones your piece, adding an additional friendly token to the board without sacrificing the original.

02

Tactical Leap

Jumping 2 distances teleports your piece to an open hex across enemy lines, vacating the initial position for surprise offensive strikes.

03

Infection Cascade

When landing, all enemy pieces touching the target destination are converted to your color instantly, triggering massive point swings.

Grandmaster Playbook

Pro Strategies & Tactical Principles

Mastering hexagonal geometry requires spatial awareness and understanding the trade-off between board growth and aggressive leaps.

Defense

Edge & Corner Anchoring

Hexes on outer perimeters have only 3 to 4 neighbors compared to 6 in the interior. Anchoring your chain along edges prevents the enemy from completely surrounding and converting your clusters.

Caution

Beware the Reckless Jump

Leaping into open enemy territory might capture 2 pieces, but leaves an isolated token exposed to counter-infections. Prefer cloning over jumping unless the capture yields a 3+ piece swing or seals an endgame cluster.

Control

Choke Points & Donut Rings

In maps like The Donut Void or Quantum Hourglass, controlling the narrow bridges cuts off the opponent's expansion, forcing them to pass turns or jump blindly into your territory.

Endgame

Chain Reaction Conversions

When the board is over 80% full, single moves can convert up to 6 adjacent hexes in one turn. Calculate multiple moves ahead to ensure your conversion cannot be immediately recaptured on the next turn.

📖

How to Play Hexxagon

1

Clone / Duplicate (Distance 1)Green Dots

Click one of your pieces and select any adjacent neighboring empty hex. A brand new piece is spawned on the target cell while keeping your original piece intact.

2

Jump / Leap (Distance 2)Amber Dots

You can leap across two spaces to reach distant tactical positions. Jumping removes the piece from its starting cell and places it at the target destination.

3

Infection / ConversionCascade Attack

Whenever your piece lands on a hex, all neighboring opponent pieces immediately get converted to your color! Strategic moves can turn 3–5 enemy pieces at once.

4

Victory Condition

The game ends when all board spaces are occupied or no player can make a legal move. The player with the highest total piece count claims victory!
